title: Predictive Microburst Assurance: Insurance-backed Reserved Pools and Graceful Degradation PRD
creator: Maya Thompson
description: This PRD proposes a new feature set for Dedicated capacity that we are calling Predictive Microburst Assurance (PMA). PMA combines predictive buffer allocation, an optional insurance-backed temporary reserved pool, and tiered graceful-degradation policies to protect paying tenants from short-duration microbursts without requiring long-lived overcommitments. The product spans API behavior, console controls, telemetry/billing changes, and rollout safety. The feature aims to reduce customer-reported latency spikes and OOM-style preemptions during high short-lived demand while keeping total cluster utilization economically efficient.
problem_statement: Many customers experience sharp, short-duration surges (microbursts) that either 1) cause request-level latency spikes when served on shared capacity or 2) trigger preemptive eviction when attempting to burst into reserved capacity. Businesses that need predictable UX (interactive apps, chatbots) are sensitive to these spikes. Existing reserved-pools and burst pathways are coarse-grained: either permanently reserve headroom (costly) or allow uncontrolled bursts that affect SLOs for other tenants. We need a way to offer affordable temporary headroom with clear governance, observability, and billing semantics.
goals: Provide a low-latency, short-duration headroom mechanism (<= 5 minutes) for Dedicated customers to cover microbursts
Expose a tenant-configurable policy that balances cost vs. availability (insurance credits, max-burst-duration, max-burst-cpu/gpu)
Ensure predictable degradation for impacted tenants and uphold critical SLOs for high-priority reserved tenants
Instrument telemetry for billing, unfairness detection, and post-incident analysis
Roll out gradually with canary tenants and automated rollback triggers
non_goals: Replace long-term reserved capacity commitments (this is complementary)
Offer unlimited burst capacity or remove standard quota protections
user_personas: Platform Engineer for an AI SaaS who wants consistent interactive latency for customers
Growth-stage engineering lead who needs predictable UX during marketing-driven traffic spikes
SRE on Redwood cust ops who will operate and troubleshoot tenant bursts
requirements: API: New optional 'microburst_policy' field on Dedicated reservation resource that accepts: insurance_enabled (boolean), credit_limit (minutes), max_concurrency_delta (tokens/GPUs), priority_tier (integer), fallback_model_variant (string)
Control plane: Scheduler must accept ephemeral allocations with TTL and enforce preemption order based on priority_tier and active credits
Console: UI panel to configure per-reservation microburst policy and show active insurance credit balance, recent burst events, and estimated cost
Telemetry: Emit events for microburst_allocate, microburst_release, microburst_preempt and metrics for burst_latency_95, burst_preempt_count, burst_credit_consumed
Billing: When insurance_enabled=true, bill pro-rated 'burst minutes' against the tenant's insurance credits and provide invoice line item summaries

Fallbacks: If insurance credits exhausted, fallback rules apply in order: 1) degrade model variant (if configured), 2) route to shared-hosted pool with latency warning, 3) reject with clear error code 429-BURST
SLOs: During a covered microburst, median P95 latency for the tenant should not exceed the negotiated SLO by more than 15% for durations <= credit_limit
Operational: Include canary gating flags, kill-switch, and automated rollback when system-level preemption rate > threshold
acceptance_criteria: Can create/update a Dedicated reservation with microburst_policy via API and Console and see policy reflected in reservation GET responses
Scheduler honors ephemeral allocations: newly requested microburst allocations are active within 12s of request under normal cluster conditions
During simulated microburst test harness (10x baseline qps for 3 minutes), a tenant with insurance_enabled=true consumes credits and maintains P95 latency within 1.15x target for >= 90% of requests
When credits are exhausted, configured fallback model variant is served for requests and an event 'microburst_fallback' is emitted
Billing records show line items for burst minutes consumed and total charge matches cost model within 2% during end-to-end test
Console shows an audit trail of allocations/releases and a time-series chart of burst_credit_balance with per-event details
Automated canary: roll to 5 pilot tenants in dedicated pools without customer impact and no system preemption spike (>5% global preemptions) within 48h
Feature flag rollback triggers if microburst_preempt_count exceeds configured safe threshold within a one-hour window
success_metrics: Reduce customer-reported latency incidents attributed to microbursts by 60% for early adopters within 30 days
Decrease emergency-support tickets about eviction during marketing spikes by 50% for pilot tenants
Average cluster utilization improvement of >=2% vs naive long-lived headroom for tenants using insurance credits
Billing adoption conversion: >=10% of pilot tenants enable insurance within 60 days
api_spec: POST /v1/dedicated/reservations -> body: {name, capacity, microburst_policy: {insurance_enabled, credit_limit_minutes, max_concurrency_delta, priority_tier, fallback_model_variant}}
POST /v1/dedicated/reservations/{id}/microburst: trigger manual allocation (admin or automated) -> returns allocation_id and TTL
ui_changes: Reservation detail page: new 'Microburst Assurance' card with toggle, slider for credit_limit (1-30 minutes), numeric input for max concurrency delta, dropdown for priority tier, and text field for fallback model
Telemetry dashboard: new 'Microburst' dashboard template with charts for credit consumption, preemptions, and burst P95 latency
Billing view: line-item drilldown for burst minutes and per-minute rate for insurance
telemetry_and_monitoring: Emit structured events (microburst_allocate, microburst_release, microburst_preempt, microburst_fallback) to centralized event pipeline
Expose metrics: burst_credit_balance_gauge, burst_minute_consumed_counter, burst_preempt_counter, burst_latency_p95_histogram
Add alerting rules: 'microburst_preempt_rate > 0.05 for 5m' and 'burst_credit_depletion_early_warning < 20% remaining'
Trace spans should include allocation_id and reservation_id for correlation
billing_and_pricing_model: Insurance pricing: fixed per-minute rate for guaranteed headroom + variable surcharge for priority_tier > 0
Invoice: include burst minutes consumed and tier surcharge; provide usage export for reconciliation
Free tier: pilot program offers 30 free burst minutes per month for selected customers
testing_plan: Load test harness: synthetic tenants that can generate controlled microbursts (10x baseline qps for up to 10 minutes)
Chaos scenarios: simulated host failures while bursts active to validate preemption ordering
Integration tests: API <-> scheduler <-> billing e2e tests that verify credits decrement and invoice entries
Canary: staged rollout to 5 tenants, monitor telemetry for 72h, then expand to 25 tenants if pass criteria met
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha (2 weeks) — feature behind flag, run internal load tests
Phase 1: Pilot (4 weeks) — invite 5 customer tenants, manual ops oversight, daily review
Phase 2: Expansion (6 weeks) — open opt-in to all Dedicated customers, automated billing enabled
Phase 3: GA — feature on by default as opt-out for new reservations (marketing announcement)
dependencies: Scheduler: ephemeral allocation API and preemption ordering (ENG-42001)
Billing: per-minute billing meters and invoice templates (ENG-50212)
Console: new UI controls and dashboard components (DES-22010)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overuse of burst credits causes cluster-level unfairness. Mitigation: global rate limiter and priority_tier enforcement; telemetry to detect unfairness and automated soft-disable
Risk: Complexity in billing causing disputes. Mitigation: clear invoice lines, exportable evidence with allocation_ids, and a 30-day pilot grace reconciliation period
Risk: Bugs in preemption ordering causing SLO regressions for high-tier tenants. Mitigation: unit tests, conservative canary, and a kill-switch tied to preemption alerts
Risk: Customers misconfigure fallback model leading to degraded UX. Mitigation: console defaults to safe fallback and warn on mismatch; validation on policy save
open_questions: Should we allow cross-reservation insurance credits (pool credits shared across multiple reservations under same org)?
What is the appropriate base per-minute price to balance revenue vs adoption?
How to present fallback behavior in SDK errors: use 429-BURST vs 200-with-warning metadata?
Do we allow negative-credit overdraft for highest-tier tenants with post-facto reconciliation?
notes: This PRD intentionally positions PMA as an insurance/adaptive headroom product rather than permanent reserve expansion. Focus early efforts on telemetry and predictable fallbacks; pricing experiments should run as A/B on pilot tenants. Close coordination with billing and scheduler teams is required before pilot launch.
